steps.title: Design the app and plan how it is built
steps.message:
Complete DESIGN.md yourself below the closing shipyard:design marker, following the
designing-the-interface skill: the scene, what this must not look like, the details and wording
of each screen. Then plan the data and the screens on top of the installed parts and their seams,
without rebuilding anything a part already does, and write the plan into .shipyard/progress.md as
the "Next" list, one line per step. Keep both short. No code in this step.

steps.title: The first real feature
steps.message:
Phase 1 of 3: The first real feature

One thing, finished properly: the screen first so you can see it, then everything behind it. It tells us the shape of the rest.

When this phase is finished, the person who owns this project should be able
to open the app and see something that was not there before. Please work
towards that rather than towards a complete data model.

This is a working prototype: the main journey has to really work, end to
end, on the real database, with real sign-in where the idea has one.
Sample rows to start from are fine; faking what the journey depends on is not.
Polish, rare cases and nice-to-haves can wait.

This project already has these ready-made parts installed. Use them rather
than writing your own, and do not edit inside their folders:

- **Signing in** — `src/components/auth`
- **The screens people sign in on** — `src/components/auth_screens`
- **A list people can sort and search** — `src/components/data_table`
- **I forgot my password** — `src/components/password_reset`
- **Database foundation** — `src/components/postgres_schema`
- **Emailing your users** — `src/components/transactional_email`
- **The screens every app starts with** — `src/components/ui_blocks`
- **How the app looks** — `src/components/ui_foundation`

If one of them is genuinely wrong for what is being asked, say so rather than
working around it.

Leave the app running at the end. If you cannot, say what is broken rather
than leaving it for the owner to discover.

Build the code and the screens yourself, each screen against DESIGN.md.

steps.title: Write the browser checks for the core flows
steps.message:
Beside e2e/smoke.spec.ts, add or update one Playwright spec per core flow in IDEA.md: what a
person does, step by step, and what they should see. They run on Shipyard's test copy of the app
(.shipyard/check-server.json), never on the founder's app; do not start a server. Each check
creates the data it needs. Run only the specs you write, one file at a time:
npx playwright test e2e/<file>.spec.ts. A failing check is a finding: fix the app, never weaken the check.

core_flow_specs_present.summary: 2 browser checks failed in the last run.

steps.title: Walk the app in a browser
steps.message:
Run the browser checks one spec file at a time against the app Shipyard is running, read the
screenshots in test-results/, and fix what is actually wrong on screen, worst first. Run the
failing spec file again after each fix.

steps.title: Security review
steps.message:
Review what was built for security yourself: input validation, what each screen and route lets a
person see and change, secrets, and anything that reads the database. Fix anything that must
change, then say in plain words what you checked and what you fixed.
